## Contribution and scope

Describe the mechanism and the exact statement or bottleneck it changes.
Identify the challenge, semantic scope, backend family and affected theorem(s).
Distinguish a local lemma, finite certificate, construction, counterexample,
independent reproduction or scoped negative result from end-to-end admission.

## Sources and credit

Record exact source commits and artifact digests, including predecessor work.
Credit reused, parallel and superseded contributions and retain their notices.
Distinguish a dependency from a comparison or attribution-only reference.
Explain any substantive AI assistance.

## Reproduction and review receipt

| Check / obligation | Exact revision or artifact digest | Command / environment | Evidence path | Who ran it / evidence origin | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | | | | Contributor-run, independently rerun, or inspected CI | |

Separate fresh reconstruction from cached artifacts and contributor reports.
State what each check establishes, any allowed assumptions, and what was not run.
Include independent controls or counterexamples that detect the relevant failure
mode. A successful finite check is evidence only for its stated scope.

## Integration obligations and remaining work

List prerequisites and downstream implications still to discharge. Explain why
the composed construction uses the same witness, actual installed tables and
artifact versions as the component certificates. Identify any interface repair
that requires recertifying dependent components. Preserve useful negative results
with their hypotheses and reproducer, even if a different approach wins.

## Arena result (if submitted)

Link the submission ID and signed judge report, challenge ID, tier and revocation
status. For measured improvements include the pinned baseline, hardware/workload
scope and confidence interval. Label local estimates as such. Leave this section
explicitly unsubmitted if there is no judge result; PR review does not grant
admission or a leaderboard score.
